message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to call out my coworker Jackson for lying about his boxing career and other things. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, Jackson claims to have been a 23-0 pro boxer, one of the best in the valley, but when I googled his name, nothing came up. That makes me think he's lying. He also talks about how he could kick anyone's ass and how he used to be in great shape before getting out of his prime and becoming flabby. I find this really annoying because I've been training in muay thai for eight years and have a good fitness level, and I don't go around bragging about it like that. We were hanging out at work, watching UFC, and he said he could KO both fighters in the match we were watching. That's when I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm 19 and half his weight. I also mentioned that nothing shows up when you google his name and challenged him to come down to my muay thai gym if he really wanted to prove himself. He got all pissy and walked out, and then I told some coworkers about it. Most of them think I'm a asshole, but a few agreed with me. So, is it right or wrong for me to call him out like that? Let's break it down. On one hand, I feel like I was standing up for myself and not letting him keep lying and bragging about things that aren't true. He was making false claims about his abilities and past, and I was just pointing out the truth. Plus, I was trying to challenge him in a way that would prove his claims, which seems fair. On the other hand, maybe I overreacted. He was just talking about himself, and while it was annoying, maybe I should have handled it differently. By calling him out in front of others and then telling coworkers about it, I might have made things worse. Now, most of my coworkers think I'm a asshole, which isn't good for workplace harmony. Also, I'm 19 and he's 29, so there's an age difference. Maybe he feels threatened or embarrassed, and that's why he got upset. I should consider his feelings and how my actions might have affected him. Another thing to think about is whether calling him out publicly was the best approach. Maybe I should have talked to him privately instead of in front of others. That way, it wouldn't have been as embarrassing for him, and it might have been more effective in getting through to him. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could have addressed his lies without being confrontational. For example, I could have asked him questions about his past to see if he could provide any evidence or details, rather than directly calling him out. Additionally, I need to consider the impact on my own reputation. By telling coworkers about the incident, I might have made myself look like someone who can't handle conflicts maturely. That's not good for building positive relationships at work. In summary, while I feel like I was standing up for myself and the truth, the way I handled the situation might have been too confrontational and hurtful. It's important to balance standing up for oneself with maintaining respectful and professional relationships in the workplace. Maybe next time, I should address the issue more calmly and privately, rather than calling someone out in front of others. That way, I can express my concerns without causing unnecessary conflict or damage to workplace relationships.
